steps.do: Create the skill that holds your customer-support response policy (tone, citations, escalation). A skill is a reusable behavior an agent can select; the one-line summary is the trigger text the selector reads, so keep it narrow. Clicking Build Skill opens the guided wizard (Identity → Content → … → Review & Create). Names must be kebab-case and must not start with claude or anthropic.
fill: Voice and citation rules for customer-facing support replies (billing, refunds, account, how-to); NOT for engineering, code, API, infra, or schema questions.
paste the body of support-tone-and-citation.md (everything below the YAML frontmatter, starting at You shape how a support reply is written...)
steps.see: The skill is created at v1 and its workspace opens with stage tabs (Author, Render Preview, Trigger Tests, Scenario Sets, Runs, Bind).

steps.do: Confirm the summary and content saved correctly, and tweak them here if needed. Editing on the Author stage is what updates the skill, so this is where the trigger summary and the policy body live.
fill: verify the trigger summary and the policy body match the asset; adjust wording if needed
steps.see: A success toast and the updated summary/content become the live skill definition.

steps.do: Check that the skill's template variables fill in cleanly. Render Preview substitutes {{ vars }} and reports any it could not resolve — supply all three required variables so nothing is left unresolved.
steps.see: A rendered reply that cites [KB-1042]/[KB-1007] and avoids a fixed date, with unresolved_variables reported as empty ([]).

steps.do: Run the positive trigger cases — customer-facing support phrasing that should select this skill. Trigger testing is deterministic (no LLM): it returns is_selected, selection_score, and selection_reason. Run rows T01–T06 from the cases file, one at a time.
fill: for each positive row, paste its user_message (e.g. How do I get a refund for the duplicate charge on my account?) from trigger-cases.jsonl
the row's session_goal (e.g. Draft a customer-facing support reply)
steps.see: Each positive case returns is_selected = true with a selection score and a human-readable reason.

steps.do: Now run the negative cases — engineering/code/API/infra/schema queries that should not select this support skill. This proves the skill is narrow and won't fire on the wrong work. Run rows T07–T12.
fill: for each negative row, paste its user_message (e.g. How do I rotate the JWT signing key without invalidating active sessions?) from trigger-cases.jsonl
steps.see: Each negative case returns is_selected = false. Tally false-positives + false-negatives across all 12 cases — the gate is trigger accuracy ≥ 0.95.

steps.do: If any negative case wrongly selected (a false positive), sharpen the summary first — the summary/trigger text dominates selection, so tighten it before touching the long-form content. (Skip this edit if all 12 cases already passed.)
fill: tighten the boundary wording, e.g. add explicit exclusions like ...NOT for engineering, code, API, infra, database, schema, or internal-tooling questions.
steps.see: The updated summary is saved; re-running the Trigger Tests now shows the previously mis-selected negative case returning is_selected = false.

steps.do: Save a passing trigger run as the baseline so the current stable trigger behavior is the reference for future changes. The Runs stage records durable runs and lets you pin one as the baseline.
steps.see: The run gets a Baseline marker in the run history, recording the known-good positive/negative trigger decisions.

steps.do: Queue a calibration job to refine the skill (the agent-free optimizer auto-provisions the target — no agent to pick). It runs in the background, so capture the queued job id rather than waiting for it to finish inline.
steps.see: A confirmation reading "Calibration queued — job {job_id}."; the job runs in the background. Note the job id.

steps.do: Export the skill as a portable package. Download ZIP lives only on the standalone skill detail page, a separate surface from the in-page Workspace (clicking a skill in the Skills list opens the Workspace stages, which have no Download ZIP). Navigate directly to /skills/<skill_id> in the address bar — copy the skill's id from the Workspace and paste it into the URL. Download ZIP produces a self-contained bundle (SKILL.md + agents/openai.yaml + bundled resources) you can move between workspaces — this is the portability artifact the lab is proving.
steps.see: A .zip file downloads containing SKILL.md and the OpenAI agent manifest. Inspect it to confirm the summary, content, and resources round-trip out cleanly.

steps.do: Bind the skill to an agent (or a workflow node) so it can be used at runtime. Binding makes the skill available to the chosen target without any extra registration.
fill: choose an agent (or workflow node) to attach the skill to
steps.see: A confirmation that support-tone-and-citation is now bound to the selected target, ready for use.
